name: Wailing Caverns
summary: Beneath the Barrens' Lushwater Oasis, trapped steam whistles through the Wailing Caverns. Springs and fissures once promised to revive Kalimdor's sun-bleached savanna. Now the caverns hold poisoned waters, twisted wildlife, and fallen disciples caught in an unnatural nightmare.

sections.title: A Noble Vision Turned Poisonous
sections.body:
The night elf druid Naralex found a vast system of underground waters and sought to restore the Barrens. Through a conduit into the Emerald Dream, he meant to draw pure primal life through the springs and turn the parched savanna into a thriving paradise.

Deep in the caverns, Naralex entered communion with the Dream, anchored by his loyal acolytes. But his sleeping mind touched the Emerald Nightmare. Corruption seized him, and his conduit became a valve pouring venom and madness into the waters.

sections.title: The Druids of the Fang
sections.body:
As the Nightmare's dark energy spread from Naralex's helpless form, his students' minds fell to madness. They forsook the tranquil wisdom of the Cenarion Circle and became the fanatical Druids of the Fang.

Their leaders, Lady Anacondra, Lord Cobrahn, Lord Pythas, and Lord Serpentis, take reptilian forms. They embrace the caverns' venomous mutation instead of fighting it, and shield their sleeping master from outside interference. They believe this twisted growth is nature's true evolution.

sections.title: The Nightmare Made Flesh
sections.body:
Breaking the Druids of the Fang's hold does not save Naralex. At Dreamer's Rock, his remaining uncorrupted disciples begin a ritual to gently rouse him from his trance. His sleeping mind thrashes, and its deepest terror erupts as Mutanus the Devourer, a monstrous, distorted murloc. Mutanus is the flesh of Naralex's worst nightmares.

Only by slaying Mutanus can the channel to the Nightmare be snapped. Naralex is freed to wake, assume avian form, and fly from the tainted caves.

faq.q: Why is it called the Wailing Caverns?
faq.answer: The Wailing Caverns take their name from the mournful cries heard in their tunnels. Trapped subterranean steam and high-pressure gusts of wind force their way through tight limestone fissures, making the eerie whistle.

faq.q: What caused the beasts inside to become 'deviate'?
faq.answer: When Naralex fell under the Emerald Nightmare's sway, tainted dream energies flowed into the underground springs. The contaminated waters mutated the raptors, crocolisks, and serpents living there into unnatural deviate forms.

faq.q: Who are the Druids of the Fang?
faq.answer: The Druids of the Fang were once Naralex's devoted night elf and tauren acolytes. Corrupted alongside him by the Nightmare, their minds shattered, and their druidic arts turned to worship of serpents and venom. They took titles such as Cobrahn, Pythas, and Anacondra.

faq.q: Why is the final boss a giant murloc named Mutanus?
faq.answer: Mutanus appears during the attempt to awaken Naralex. The ritual reveals Mutanus's nature and connection to the sleeping druid.

faq.q: What happens after Mutanus is defeated?
faq.answer: The disciples' attempt to awaken Naralex continues after the confrontation. The ritual reveals the druid's fate at its end.

faq.q: Who is living in the cave above the cavern entrance?
faq.answer: Cenarion Circle loyalists, including Nalpak and Ebru, live in the cavern's skull-like rock eye socket above the entrance. They seek brave travelers to gather deviate hides and cleanse the corruption before it engulfs the Barrens.

angles.text: For druids of both Cenarion tradition and the tauren walk, the caverns are a tragic warning of the perils within the Emerald Dream. Purging their fallen brethren, the Druids of the Fang, is a solemn duty.
The twisted waters threaten the fragile oases that sustain life across the Barrens. Cleansing the springs is vital to the tribes of Mulgore and the Crossroads.
Naralex was revered among night elf druids. His corruption by the Emerald Nightmare is a painful catastrophe for his kin across the sea.
